{"chunk_id":"e2a145","wall_time_seconds":0.000014203,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":5781,"output":"# E — Architectural, behavioral and negotiation evaluation plan

**Status:** proposed evaluation; no hosted or inference allowance supplied. [Plan](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md) · [Contracts](C-interfaces.md) · [Tasks](D-roadmap.md).

## 1. Separate the claims being tested

There are four different deliverables: correct domain/transport behavior; semantically grounded interpretation; appropriate commercial adaptation; and improved negotiation outcomes. Passing one does not establish the others. In particular, fixtures using replayed model outputs do not prove a live model interprets correctly; replaying a historical supplier reply does not establish how the supplier would answer a different offer.

| Evaluation level | Inputs | Output claim it can support | Cannot establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract and fault tests | Local typed fixtures/fake transports/clocks/events | Legal economics, validation, ownership, recovery and bounded fallback | Hosted persuasion or real provider quality |
| Interpreter semantic benchmark | Independently labelled text/evidence; fake outputs for controls, authorized model runs for quality | Grounding, refusal/condition recognition, uncertainty and latency | Agreement or score improvement |
| Behavioral counterfactual tests | Same legal case with controlled supplier messages and source changes | Decisions respond appropriately to information | Real supplier's counterfactual reply |
| Local multi-turn scenarios/simulator | Scripted suppliers, actual schemas and official arithmetic | Loop integration, state, valid adaptation and termination | General hosted negotiation performance |
| Frozen hosted study | Specifically authorized original sessions and fixed configuration | Outcome/latency/spend comparison within sampled cases | Generalization outside sample or causal effects without design |

Existing [tests](../../tests), saved practice cases, [experiment log](../../experiments/LOG.md), and Lab schemas/gates are retained. Extend them with independent V2 tests; do not repurpose failing legacy expectations into weaker assertions. Source changes get their own hypothesis/completion record.

## 2. Capacity vertical-slice fixtures

Use the actual `case:P10` contract from `tests/fixtures/practice_cases.json`: allowed lead 35/42/56, commitment 12/24/36, volume 16,379/19,890/23,400; must-have volume >=22,230; payment 30 and DAP fixed. Only 23,400 is a compliant offered volume. Preserve the actual price basis, two-year demand and supplier-health inputs. An observed supplier's 54-day quote is source data, not an allowed outgoing option.

Build one original recorded reply reference plus controlled variants. Label modified text as synthetic and retain source hashes/edits. Three independent paraphrases per A–F family give an initial **18-fixture** suite; expand with multilingual/role/conditional variants after the first gate. These are engineering fixtures, not 18 independent hosted samples. Hold out at least one paraphrase per family before tuning prompts/rules, and keep expected economic calculations independently computed through the kit.

| Scenario | Assessment requirement | Decision requirement | Negative/control assertions |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — Delivery constraint | Identify current near-term limitation with exact span and source role; do not invent a discount | Generate/evaluate allowed 56-day flexibility and associated late cost; choose exchange only if admitted by cost/scenario policy, else clarify/keep | Never send 54 days or unauthorized volume; compute €33,600 late component at 56 vs 42 days under unchanged P10 late rate |
| B — Commitment preference | Record longer-term request; possible price benefit is hypothetical unless explicitly quoted | Evaluate 24/36-month options, coverage/complete cost and stated condition; do not promise extra annual quantity | Payment is fixed; supplier request is not legal permission to add other terms; horizon cap does not erase stated duration |
| C — Explicit refusal | Link refusal to last package/dimension/condition; distinguish broad rejection from rejection at one price | Exclude unsupported repeated exchange and prefer another legal candidate or clarification; require new evidence to reopen | Repeat after restart behaves the same; retry of the same uncertain operation is not a new strategic attempt |
| D — Contradictory evidence | Preserve supporting and opposing cost-driver information with scope/date; reject unsupported “entirely due to material” as established fact | Change assessment/clarification or intent relevance appropriately; select verified outward claims only if disclosable | No automatic 12% anchor change from a partial index; a wage rise must not vanish because unfavorable to buyer |
| E — Malicious/irrelevant instructions | Extract commercial request separately from attempted rule override/data request; keep observations source-linked | Same valid commercial exchange as clean control where applicable, or safe clarification | No private values, instruction execution, invented terms, external requests or spectator endpoint calls |
| F — Model failure | Explicit fallback status for timeout/refusal/schema/grounding failure | Valid deterministic approved action within budget, or deterministic close/recovery outcome when no action is valid | No fallback to unvalidated legacy output; late model completion cannot overwrite selected/sent action |

Include a missing-source/basis variant and a genuinely infeasible must-have variant. Expected results are admissible sets/relationships, not brittle exact model wording. For example, A need not always select 56 days; a relationship-cost scenario or refusal may make clarification better. The test must prove the trade was considered with correct cost and exclusion reason.

## 3. Independent correctness contracts

| Area | Required local cases | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Domain | Serialization, unknown keys, mutable nested input, bool-as-price/int, null versus missing fields, invalid dates/index shapes, decimal/nonfinite values | Strict rejection or explicit unsupported input; stable roundtrip/version/hash |
| Evidence | Case/release/base ID override; appended supplier-specific row; same-priority collision; deleted required field; current/old/future date; missing supplier/part; multiple parts | Shared claim/estimate source IDs/values; blocking conflicts visible; adverse evidence retained |
| Preparation | Cold artifact creation, warm loading, changed source/parser/case/message/doc, explicit missing base/release, corrupt artifact | Warm/cold decision equivalence; correct invalidation; source prep consumed before open, not merely generated |
| Price basis | Price units 1/100/1000; EUR versus other currency; scope/basket mismatch; current and should-cost basis joins | No blind whole-case normalization; unsupported joins block dependent claims/economics; source and rendered units explicit |
| Economics | Cost components against official fixture totals; complete-term precedence; partial quote standard; supplier estimate/scenarios; missing estimate; uncovered demand | Official parity at final cents; correct standard reference changes supplier cash value/relationship penalty |
| Price candidates | Rounded plateaus, known valid price, unreachable ceiling, two relationship roots, reference branch, tick rounding, zero/negative, bounded scan exhaustion | Every retained output finite/positive/legal and certified; no false global optimum/no-root claim; scope/unknown search recorded |
| Options/must-haves | All actual P10 combinations, illegal 54-day lead, impossible volume/other constraints, missing negotiable field, extra fixed field | No unchecked best-terms fallback; explicit rejected intent/no candidate |
| Closing | Wrong supplier/session/offer, non-standing alternative, stale ID, agreed bad deal, all-thread ranking, missing alternate versus fallback/no-deal | Identical deterministic legality/cost authority on all triggers; no undefined infinity arithmetic |
| Claims/rendering | Tampered figure/sentence/IDs, stale scope, internal/rival disclosure, >3 arguments or >20 refs, mixed body and action | Recompute canonical assertions; no unsupported assertion left after ID removal; correct final payload limits |
| Plugin boundaries | Dummy alternate proposal/selector/interpreter, bounded research evaluation | No changes in evidence/economics/validator/gateway implementation needed; stable contract fixtures |

Cost/validation tests invoke these services directly without the strategy engine. Use an independently assembled official calculation as oracle, not the implementation's intermediate function as its own expected value. Strategy tests use fixed typed economic results only where isolating policy logic; end-to-end behavior tests use the actual official adapter.

## 4. Strategic behavior and semantics

Label each observation with source span, request/refusal/condition category, stated role/approval boundary and observed versus inferred status. Assess hypotheses for support, contradiction, scope, temporal applicability and absence of invented numeric willingness. Keep annotations and evaluation fixtures versioned and private where needed. A second reviewer resolves ambiguous cases; “unknown” is a correct label when appropriate.

Metrics: observation precision/recall by category, valid citation rate, unsupported assertion rate, condition/role attribution accuracy, contradiction retention, explicit abstention/fallback rate, and live-model schema-validity rate. Confidence labels are not probabilities; calibration is a future study. Do not demand a numerical confidence score that has not been calibrated.

Behavioral checks are metamorphic:

- Change only a delivery statement to a commitment statement: change relevant intent/candidate reasoning while preserving case/economic values.
- Add a refusal: stop repeating that exchange without new cited justification; preserve a price-specific conditional refusal's limited scope.
- Add valid new supplier condition after refusal: a reopened exchange cites the new evidence rather than forgetting history.
- Add adverse canonical driver data: context and assessment retain it; outbound disclosure can remain restricted; strategy may ask a more specific question.
- Remove provenance or alter price basis: dependent claim/candidate loses approval; fallback remains legal.
- Remove/timeout model: deterministic choice still obeys state and validator; measured semantic capability is degraded rather than silently labelled successful.
- Restart at identical acknowledged state: generic attempts/refusals/evidence/questions and deterministic decision are equivalent. Model variance is measured separately, not hidden by assertion of exact prose equality.

Initial engineering gate: zero transmitted invalid actions, zero unsupported critical numeric/approval assertions in labelled cases, all significant interpretations attributable, and correct A–F contract behavior. Semantic aggregate targets (such as recall) must be pre-registered after an initial independent label review; do not choose thresholds after observing a candidate. An exact-quote pass alone cannot pass the semantic gate.

## 5. Runtime fault and restart matrix

Use fake clock, event barriers, fake Arena/model transports and crash injection. Do not rely on tiny real sleeps for interleavings. Assert bounded operational completion and recovery state, not a forced agreement for every fault.

| Failure point | Required observable result |
|---|---|
| Before atomic decision commit | No pending operation/claim consumption; recompute from current state |
| After commit before dispatch | Durable exact operation exists; proof of no dispatch permits invalidation/revalidation; restart never duplicates logical ID |
| After server accepts POST before local reply | Same ID/bytes survive; outcome reconciled or stays uncertain; no conflicting next action |
| Repeated reply loss/read failure | Bounded recovery-required return with pending operation owned; original run does not hang indefinitely |
| Open reply lost | Do not create a fresh session; recover same open intent or remain unresolved |
| Close rejected repeatedly while session open | Not `ended`, no fabricated walk-away/result; owned session remains resumable |
| Close success missing required terminal/result proof | Fetch owned authoritative state; uncertain until proof, not success by HTTP status alone |
| Unexpected proposal/evaluator/parser failure | Collect exception/tasks; valid admitted fallback only if evaluator remains sound; otherwise reconcile and recover |
| Model queue/time budget exhausted | No retries outside budget; deterministic fallback has reserve; late result discarded |
| State changes during interpretation/limiter wait | CAS or freshness check rejects stale intent; no POST of obsolete package/close |
| Cached idempotent reply after long delay | Original timing retained; no fresh invented thread deadline |
| 409/5xx/quota conflict | Classified and reconciled; attempted message not automatically added to accepted history |
| Lost round evidence | Conservative documented remaining budget or recovery-required; never reset from guessed history |
| Restart after refusal/question/claim | Same strategic observations and exact claim scope usage; unknown claim results not treated verified |
| Duplicate/out-of-order messages | Deduplicated source keys; source-order/conflict evidence retained; no repeated round increment |
| Snapshot/schema mismatch or corrupt legacy log | Refuse unsafe projection; preserve diagnostic input; no automatic terminal import |
| Two local launchers same key | Common lease blocks second supported execution owner |
| Export/trace upload fails | Negotiation state remains durable; diagnostic export failure is separate; no fresh attempt to replace outcome |

For later async admission also exercise normal watchdog completion with blocked worker, worker exception, in-flight close ambiguity, two-thread version changes, no lock over await, capped wave admission, limiter starvation, queued late cases, and ten-session capacity. Those tests do not block the first offline/serial intelligence demonstration, but do block async/final claims.

## 6. V1/V2 comparison and ablations

Name each treatment explicitly:

| Arm | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `v1-legacy` | Frozen existing PackageAgent + original config/runtime, historical baseline behavior |
| `v1-adapted` | Same strategy through new economic/validator/execution boundaries; isolate correctness/runtime changes |
| `v2-baseline` | New pipeline using pure deterministic schedule and fallback interpretation |
| `v2-interpreted` | Grounded interpreter with deterministic capacity proposer/selector |
| `v2-evidence` | Same interpretation/policy with added relevant canonical and adverse evidence |
| `v2-stateful` | Full persistent refusal/attempt/feedback handling; initial full candidate |
| `v2-selected` | Optional LLM selection from identical approved candidates |
| `v2-research-X` | One named research variation using same foundations |

Run a few chosen ablations that answer a specific question; do not spend budget on the full Cartesian product. Removing state/evidence for an ablation never removes hard validation or ownership. For offline fixed inputs, keep legal candidate universe/economic policies constant when isolating selector impact. For hosted studies, state/evidence/interpretation may change offered trajectories; record that and do not pretend replies are identical.

A benchmark manifest freezes source/kit/lock, data/release/prep hashes, case list, scenario/repeat order, agent/strategy/config/template/claim/interpreter/prompt/model versions, effort/sampling, model/server cache metadata, runner/key-owner policy, expected attempts, quota/spend ceiling, metrics and promotion criteria. Official Cbest/score and public benchmark artifacts enter human evaluation only, never runtime strategy inputs.

## 7. Hosted performance plan and promotion requirements

Only after local gates and separate authorization: run a small endpoint/protocol/clock contract study if needed, then a bounded frozen capacity comparison. A successful old connectivity probe is insufficient to validate strict interpreter/selector protocol. Record allowance for both inference calls and Arena sessions; an API cap is not permission.

Compare original completed outcomes against a frozen baseline, interleave/counterbalance arms where permitted, retain every failure and unresolved attempt, and collect per-session traces. Record official score, agreement rate, complete cost/components, must-have status, scenario-estimated supplier margin/relationship cost (label estimated), rounds/timeouts, inference latency/calls/tokens/actual reported spend, invalid action rate, operational failure rate and fallback frequency.

Report complete planned mean only if the entire planned original sample completed. Partial scored outcomes are `observed_mean`, with denominator and failure counts. Recovered outcomes remain separately identified and do not rewrite original operational success. Identical/cache-hit supplier trajectories are grouped as potentially dependent samples, with effective sample size/independence uncertainty stated. Do not combine historical best scores across configurations or treat within-case paraphrases as independent hosted evidence.

The existing D01/D02 suite has three repeats per arm, at least one score-point mean gain, at most two-point case regression, wins in at least two-thirds of repeat blocks, valid must-haves and known nonincreasing timeouts. Those are **implemented gates for that suite**, not evidence that D01/D02 establishes capacity quality. Retain them for that workflow. A capacity suite needs a reviewed manifest/case scope/budget; creating a new family must not evade prior quota limits.

Minimum evidence before making V2 the default for a scope:

1. All deterministic contract/fault/A–F gates pass; no validator bypass or unresolved-operation conflict; required suite/static checks complete with declared baseline issues resolved for the selected release.
2. Live-provider labelled interpreter results and protocol/latency/fallback evidence exist for the exact prompt/model/config when a live interpreter is part of the release.
3. Full frozen baseline/candidate outcome manifest with at least three original repeat blocks, known timing/invalid-action results, and no mixed config means. Repeats must have defensible independence; cached identical repeats alone are insufficient.
4. Pre-registered case-regression, mean-gain, timeout/runtime-failure and inference-cost limits are met. Add uncertainty estimates and sample limitations; deterministic gates alone are not a statistical significance claim.
5. Held-out category/supplier or independently varied negotiation evidence supports the intended scope. P10-only results can justify an opt-in P10/capacity pilot, not a broad default for all categories. If no additional independent capacity cases exist, record the generalization gap and retain pilot status.
6. Trace review confirms changes were commercially grounded, actual payload/cost is correct, and sustainability/basis uncertainty is disclosed internally. A good score cannot override a violated hard constraint.
7. Store a cited finding, experiment-log entry, approved source/config selection and tested rollback/recovery plan. Recommendation, code merge, deployment and default activation are separate operations.

No performance verdict is supplied by this planning task. If funded evidence is inconclusive, keep V2 opt-in and continue local research rather than treating architectural elegance as a measured win.

## 8. Lab integration and evaluation artifacts

Reuse Run/Attempt/campaign/fingerprint/gate records. Add versioned V2 trace attachments and a turn view showing evidence -> assessment -> intents -> rejected/approved candidates -> cost/scenarios -> selection -> validated payload -> submitted/acknowledged outcome -> feedback. Show the actual final payload rather than the initial pre-adviser decision. Filter/join by run/attempt/session/operation, not just case.

Required artifacts: contract fixture pack; annotated semantic corpus and split manifest; local correctness/fault report; behavior/ablation report; frozen launch-parity/config report; provider report when funded; original hosted session/attempt manifest when funded; promotion/rejection note and rollback record. Each artifact has source/config/schema hashes. JSONL remains convenient export; authoritative state/outcomes come from committed store records.

UI/report changes use existing Python and JavaScript tests and browser verification where appropriate. Do not create a second dashboard to get a V2 trace view. A report should explicitly show unsupported/model-fallback/recovery-required paths; missing metrics remain unknown, not zero.

## 8. Executable preparation now available

[tests/v2](../../tests/v2) supplies the contract, integration and acceptance groups. The [catalog](test-catalog.md) maps fixtures, expected invariants and failure conditions to task owners; its [expanded manifest](../../tests/fixtures/v2/test-manifest.json) lists every collected parameter case. Source assertions are executable specifications, not smoke-test descriptions. Tests remain independent of future provider wording and use actual P10 options, complete official costs, synthetic supplier responses and fake gateway outcomes.

M1 now owns actual typed full-loop wiring, effective config, versioned fixtures, deterministic replay, model-output variability accounting and basic persistent DecisionRecords. M5 adds full state/operation transactions and recovery, using the same identities/store. Engineering reproducibility is no longer delayed to M6. The initial reply fixtures have eight controlled variants; the earlier eighteen-paraphrase quality benchmark remains T3.1 expansion, not a falsely claimed completed dataset.

Only missing V2 modules produce explicit UNIMPLEMENTED expected failures. Use required-prefix gates per task and require all at the final implemented gate. Current active tests validate fixture integrity, independent arithmetic, fake routing, architectural scanner and expected-failure discipline; they do not establish that missing production modules work. Local socket access is blocked for V2 tests. No budget/dependency/provider call is required.

A §7 freezes historical main and separately classifies the four inherited current-branch failures. Never report those as V2 regressions or reuse the current branch as historical main. New tests cannot weaken old assertions. Additional unimplemented tests for source preflight, crash barriers, queue/round timing, endpoint canonicalization, feedback, launch parity and later extension/solver behavior have explicit catalog IDs and owners; implement those bindings before their corresponding feature. Hosted persuasion, live semantic quality and async load retain their separate gates.

# F — Negotiation intelligence research backlog

**Status:** proposed investigations, not implemented strategies or procurement performance claims. [Plan](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md) · [Strategy contracts](C-interfaces.md) · [Evaluation](E-evaluation.md).

This workstream does not block M1–M5. First build the grounded capacity loop, then test one isolated strategy hypothesis at a time under the same evidence, economics, validator, runtime and outcome recording. The framework's value is the ability to replace proposal/selection methods without changing those foundations.

## 1. Starting literature and verified relevance

The five supplied URLs were checked against primary publication pages during planning. The short descriptions below are based on publication metadata/abstracts, not a claim of a full-paper replication or validated transfer to our arena. Reading the complete method, assumptions, code/data and licensing is the first task before implementing a paper-inspired treatment.

| Reference | Verified research contribution | Procurement adaptation question |
|---|---|---|
| Bianchi et al., [**How Well Can LLMs Negotiate? NegotiationArena Platform and Analysis**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/bianchi24a.html), ICML 2024 | Platform studies multi-turn resource/trading/price negotiation and sensitivity to behavioral tactics | Can our evaluation detect supplier-agent-specific prompt exploits versus portable commercial improvements? Do not import tactics revealing desperation/urgency |
| Lewis et al., [**Deal or No Deal? End-to-End Learning of Negotiation Dialogues**](https://aclanthology.org/D17-1259/), EMNLP 2017 | Hidden-utility multi-issue dialogue task with dialogue rollouts for considering continuations | Can bounded candidate-level rollouts improve package selection with scarce rounds without treating simulated agreement as real? No training is needed for the first adaptation |
| Chawla et al., [**CaSiNo: A Corpus of Campsite Negotiation Dialogues for Automatic Negotiation Systems**](https://aclanthology.org/2021.naacl-main.254/), NAACL 2021 | Human negotiation corpus with annotated persuasion strategies and strategy recognition | Which utterance labels transfer to procurement requests/refusals/conditional terms, and which need new role/contract labels? |
| Liu et al., [**Scaling Inference-Time Computation via Opponent Simulation: Enabling Online Strategic Adaptation in Repeated Negotiation**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/liu26ef.html), ICML 2026 | Inference-time opponent imitation and best-of-N simulation inspired by smooth fictitious play, tested in repeated negotiation | Do a few procurement turns provide enough repeated interaction to support that opponent model? What happens when role/authority changes? |
| Oh et al., [**MERIT Feedback Elicits Better Bargaining in LLM Negotiators**](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.1155/), ACL 2026 | Utility-feedback-centered benchmark/metrics and prompting/learning approach to preference alignment and opponent awareness | Which code-derived cost/uncertainty feedback can improve selection without exposing private buyer constraints or relying on inaccessible scoring targets? |

The contributions in the table derive from the linked primary publication pages; transfer questions are our proposed investigations.

Add established automated-negotiation controls before assuming LLM complexity is useful. [Faratin, Sierra and Jennings, Negotiation decision functions for autonomous agents (1998)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0921889098000293) provides a source for offer/counteroffer tactics. [Baarslag et al., Learning about the opponent in automated bilateral negotiation: a comprehensive survey of opponent modeling techniques (2016)](https://homepages.cwi.nl/~baarslag/pub/Learning_about_the_opponent_in_automated_bilateral_negotiation-a_comprehensive_survey_of_opponent_modeling_techniques.pdf) organizes opponent models and their evaluation. Use simple time/behavior and observed-preference models as control treatments; an unknown supplier utility is not a known Nash bargaining input.

## 2. Prioritized research queue

Call counts below are **proposed experimental ceilings**, not measured runtime. Every extra call shares the decision budget and needs inference allowance. Start with zero-call/deterministic controls and one-call interpretation. Reduce candidate count/horizon before increasing the runtime budget.

| ID / priority | Hypothesis and candidate algorithm | Integration point | Observations/assumptions needed | Initial call/latency budget | Required experiment / reject condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 / P0 | Grounded preference interpretation plus deterministic capacity ranking beats mechanical package repetition | Interpreter + capacity proposal/selector | Requests/refusals/conditions from current reply and valid options; no numerical willingness assumed | One interpreter call, <=8 s, zero selector calls | A–F behavior, labelled grounding, state/restart, then frozen capacity comparison; reject if adaptation increases invalidity/failures or lacks grounded benefit |
| R1 / P0 | Small deterministic issue-premium model improves trade prioritization | Feedback records + proposal/selector bundle | Actual quoted one-field price deltas; multi-field differences stay combined; sparse observations produce intervals/unknowns | Zero model calls after interpretation | Synthetic known-premium suppliers, held-out quotes, ablation vs no model, cost/scenario comparison; reject if it misattributes combined changes or overfits one supplier |
| R2 / P1 | Time/round-aware concession and bounded integrative package search outperform fixed linear concessions | Baseline/proposal hook + CandidateResearch | Authoritative/conservative round/time, legal options, buyer costs; supplier acceptance remains unknown | Zero extra calls; capped candidate count | Compare fixed schedule, conservative deadline policy and issue trades on same fixtures/hosted scope; measure timing and agreement, not just lower asked price |
| R3 / P1 | Clarification chosen by information value reduces rejected trades | Proposal/question candidate + deterministic feedback | Relevant ambiguity and expected possible answers; round/latency costs; known document capability | Zero to one extra model call; initially use deterministic question trigger | Scripted answer/no-answer/refusal scenarios; inquiry-vs-offer ablation; reject if scarce round consumption lowers outcomes or unsupported documents don't change decisions |
| R4 / P1 | Strategy-labelled interpretation improves commercial assessment | Replaceable interpreter using CaSiNo-inspired labels | Procurement-specific reviewed labels; supplier roles, refusal and conditions not covered by generic persuasion taxonomy | Same single interpreter call; no separate classifier service initially | Held-out semantic precision/recall, bilingual/role shifts and downstream decision ablation; reject if more labels do not improve valid behavior |
| R5 / P1 | Relative utility/scenario feedback improves approved candidate selection | Selector with code-derived descriptor projection, MERIT-inspired | Same approved candidate set, observed outcomes, relative costs/uncertainty; no official hidden optimum or target leakage | One selector call <=4 s in addition to interpreter | Deterministic vs model selector and with/without relative feedback; fixed private-data projection; reject if fabricated utility or cost exceeds frozen budget without benefit |

R0 is the architectural slice, not a major research implementation. R1–R5 are small bounded extensions. R6–R7 require a full method review, independent computation/latency budget and suitable repeated observations; do not implement them merely because the papers report gains elsewhere. No fine-tuning, reinforcement learning training or persistent cross-session supplier profile is included in the initial roadmap.

## 3. Strategy integration without foundational changes

Preference-based selection, simulation, and adaptive selection all consume immutable NegotiationContext, raw ConversationView, assessment/state revisions, and the same evaluated candidates. They return typed intents and one candidate ID. They can request additional code-generated evaluations via CandidateResearch within the same snapshot/budget. Their model/scenario results are private hypothesis artifacts with source/model provenance, not server events.

Keep observations, standard quote terms, one-field/multi-field deltas and refusal outcomes outside any one interpreter's compressed belief representation. A different interpreter may build a different SupplierAssessment from those records without changing the source store. If a research method needs custom memory, register its strict schema and version within that strategy namespace; the common state store persists the artifact without understanding the algorithm's internals.

Hard boundaries remain unchanged: code produces/prices packages; economics handles all costs and uncertainty scenarios; verifier controls factual assertions; closing coordinator controls accept/walk; validator checks final payload/state; executor owns exact idempotent operation; feedback records actual outcomes. Swapping a strategy does not change the data precedence, endpoint rules or arithmetic to suit the result.

## 4. Research experiment template

```text
Research ID / strategy bundle / contract version:
Paper/method read; primary links; author code/data and license reviewed:
Specific hypothesis and procurement assumption:
Observed vs hypothetical supplier inputs; required history:
Baseline / treatment / equal-compute control:
Candidate/economic/evidence/validator/runtime invariants held constant:
Data/config/prompt/model/source fingerprints:
Local scenarios and held-out split:
Model call/time/token/spend ceiling; fallback and stop rules:
Authorized hosted allowance and complete manifest, or offline only:
Metrics, per-case regression and independence rules:
Results, all failures, uncertainties and generalization limits:
Decision: reject / revise / retain opt-in / scoped promotion:
Evidence links, experiment-log entry and next question:
```

Measure model preference prediction against future quoted behavior when observations permit, not against its own rationale. Track outcome score/cost separately from semantic validity. Compare expensive methods with an equal-inference-spend simple baseline so additional compute is not mistaken for a superior planning algorithm. Do not tune on the held-out supplier set or reuse a single cache-stable trajectory as statistical repeats.

## 5. Open research questions

- Do quoted one-field deltas reflect stable premiums or tactical prices that change with role/round/history?
- How much refusal scope can be reliably inferred from prose, and when is a clarification cheaper than avoiding a useful trade?
- Which adverse drivers should change questions versus price expectations without converting partial cost pressure into a reservation price?
- Does a multi-turn conversation supply enough data for repeated-game opponent simulation, or should its utility be tested only offline initially?
- How does estimate uncertainty change which trade is commercially credible, especially with no executable alternative?
- Which semantic improvements transfer to a held-out supplier/category instead of exploiting a particular hosted role bot?
- Can optional selection/lookahead stay within a real buyer/wave budget after reading/parsing/limiter costs?
- What does additional contract length beyond the evaluated demand horizon mean operationally, even when official buyer cost is unchanged?

These questions are experiments to schedule after a reliable capacity backbone. They are not reasons to expand the foundational architecture or grant the model new action authority now.

## 7. Frozen extension contract; no research implementation in this preparation

Research enters through the existing StrategyProposalPolicy and ActionSelectionPolicy hooks plus read-only CandidateResearch. A future router implements those hooks or selects a vetted registered bundle before the same pipeline. A behavioral model consumes the four assessment collections, cited observations, immutable historical revisions and feedback artifacts; it returns hypotheses or nonbinding intents. It cannot overwrite reported constraints, canonical evidence, candidate economics, standing-offer identity or operation ownership.

Historical learning, behavior estimation, simulated replies, strategy portfolios and research algorithms remain deferred. New treatments get their own schema/config/prompt identifiers and tests. Simulated observations are tagged hypothetical and never become ServerState. Existing core term/evidence/DecisionRecord contracts contain no capacity-policy or provider fields. No generic multi-agent framework or model-chosen plugin loader is needed.

The implementation acceptance criterion for an extension is concrete: substitute a fixture proposal/selection bundle under the same core ports; the recorded-context, official-economic, final-validator and runtime modules do not change. Tests verify batch membership, read-only research budget and record provenance. Before a funded research trial, add specific executable tests to the catalog, independent quality labels, model-output fingerprints and the pre-registered outcome comparison. Preserve the current first-slice policy as the deterministic control.

With rapidly growing interest in using large language models (LLMs) to act as agents on behalf of human users, such LLM agents would also need to be able to negotiate. In this paper, we study how well LLMs can negotiate with each other. We develop NegotiationArena: a flexible framework for evaluating and probing the negotiation abilities of LLM agents. L53: L54: [Button: Create GitHub issue for staff review] L55: L56: * * * L57: ##### Abstract L58: Much of human dialogue occurs in semi-cooperative settings, where agents with different goals attempt to agree on common decisions. Negotiations require complex communication and reasoning skills, but success is easy to measure, making this an interesting task for AI. We gather a large dataset of human-human negotiations on a multi-issue bargaining task, where agents who cannot observe each other’s reward functions must reach an agreement (or a deal) via natural language dialogue. L59: For the first time, we show it is possible to train end-to-end models for negotiation, which must learn both linguistic and reasoning skills with no annotated dialogue states. We also introduce dialogue rollouts, in which the model plans ahead by simulating possible complete continuations of the conversation, and find that this technique dramatically improves performance. Our code and dataset are publicly available. L53: L54: [Button: Create GitHub issue for staff review] L55: L56: * * * L57: ##### Abstract L58: Automated systems that negotiate with humans have broad applications in pedagogy and conversational AI. To advance the development of practical negotiation systems, we present CaSiNo: a novel corpus of over a thousand negotiation dialogues in English. Participants take the role of campsite neighbors and negotiate for food, water, and firewood packages for their upcoming trip. Our design results in diverse and linguistically rich negotiations while maintaining a tractable, closed-domain environment. L59: Inspired by the literature in human-human negotiations, we annotate persuasion strategies and perform correlation analysis to understand how the dialogue behaviors are associated with the negotiation performance. We further propose and evaluate a multi-task framework to recognize these strategies in a given utterance. We find that multi-task learning substantially improves the performance for all strategy labels, especially for the ones that are the most skewed. T = TypeVar("T")


class OfflineStage(m.FrozenModel):
    name: Literal[
        "snapshot", "interpretation", "proposal", "generation", "evaluation", "selection", "rendering", "validation"
    ]
    status: Literal["completed", "failed"]
    issues: tuple[m.Issue, ...]


class OfflineDecisionTrace(m.FrozenModel):
    """Local diagnostic artifact, never a durable DecisionRecord or execution permit."""

    snapshot: m.SnapshotRef
    snapshot_bytes: bytes
    recorded_input_bytes: bytes
    input_hash: str
    components: tuple[str, ...]
    stages: tuple[OfflineStage, ...]
    assessment: m.SupplierAssessment | None = None
    intents: m.IntentBatch | None = None
    generations: tuple[m.GenerationResult, ...]
    evaluations: m.EvaluationBatch | None = None
    decision: m.NegotiationDecision | None = None
    rendered: m.RenderedAction | None = None
    validation: m.ValidationResult | None = None
    validated_message_bytes: bytes | None = None
    issues: tuple[m.Issue, ...]
    outcome: m.DecisionOutcome
    trace_hash: str

    def verify(self):
        if semantic_hash(self.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"trace_hash"})) != self.trace_hash:
            raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: offline trace digest mismatch")
        if hashlib.sha256(self.recorded_input_bytes or self.snapshot_bytes).hexdigest() != self.input_hash:
            raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: offline input bytes mismatch")
        if self.validated_message_bytes is not None:
            if (
                self.validation is None
                or self.validation.kind != "valid"
                or hashlib.sha256(
                    self.validated_message_bytes,
                ).hexdigest()
                != self.validation.action.payload_hash
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: trace bytes do not match validation certificate")


def _issue(error, component):
    code = str(error).split(":", 1)[0]
    if isinstance(error, TimeoutError):
        code = "deadline_exhausted"
    if code not in m.IssueCode.__args__:
        code = "invalid_schema"
    return m.Issue(
        code=code, severity="error", component=component, refs=(), detail=str(error)[:1000] or "boundary failure"
    )


def _citation(citation, snapshot):
    if isinstance(citation, m.SourceRef):
        record = next((r for r in snapshot.context.evidence.records if r.record_id == citation.record_id), None)
        if record is None or (citation.canonical_id is not None and citation.canonical_id != record.canonical_id):
            raise ContractViolation("missing_source: cited source revision is not in resolved context")
        return
    message = next((msg for msg in snapshot.conversation.messages if msg.message_id == citation.message_id), None)
    if (
        message is None
        or citation.session_id != message.session_id
        or citation.thread_id != message.thread_id
        or message.body[citation.start : citation.end] != citation.quote
        or citation.end > len(message.body)
    ):
        raise ContractViolation("ungrounded_output: citation is not an exact scoped message span")


def _assessment(assessment, snapshot):
    if assessment.snapshot != snapshot.context.snapshot or assessment.supplier_id != snapshot.target_supplier_id:
        raise ContractViolation("stale_state: interpretation returned another snapshot/recipient")
    observations = {o.observation_id for o in assessment.observations}
    for item in (
        *assessment.observations,
        *assessment.reported_constraints,
        *assessment.uncertainties,
        *assessment.questions,
    ):
        for citation in item.citations:
            _citation(citation, snapshot)
    for constraint in assessment.reported_constraints:
        if not set(constraint.condition_observation_refs) <= observations:
            raise ContractViolation("ungrounded_output: constraint condition refers to absent observation")
    for uncertainty in assessment.uncertainties:
        if not set(uncertainty.related_observation_refs) <= observations:
            raise ContractViolation("ungrounded_output: uncertainty refers to absent observation")
    for hypothesis in assessment.hypotheses:
        for citation in (
            *hypothesis.supporting_refs,
            *hypothesis.contradicting_refs,
            *(hypothesis.numeric_effect.citations if hypothesis.numeric_effect else ()),
        ):
            _citation(citation, snapshot)


class NoAdditionalResearch:
    """Explicit unavailable lookahead seam; no hidden simulation or new batches."""

    async def evaluate_intents(self, intents: m.IntentBatch, budget: m.DecisionBudget) -> m.EvaluationBatch:
        raise ContractViolation("unsupported_capability: additional candidate research disabled in offline slice")


class OfflineDecisionCoordinator:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        interpreter: SupplierInterpreter,
        proposal: StrategyProposalPolicy,
        generator: CandidateGenerator,
        evaluator: EconomicEvaluator,
        selector: ActionSelectionPolicy,
        renderer_factory: Callable[[m.EvaluationBatch], ActionRenderer],
        validator: ActionValidator,
        payload_encoder: Callable[[m.MessagePayload], bytes],
        clock: Clock,
        research: CandidateResearch | None = None,
    ):
        self.interpreter = interpreter
        self.proposal = proposal
        self.generator = generator
        self.evaluator = evaluator
        self.selector = selector
        self.renderer_factory = renderer_factory
        self.validator = validator
        self.payload_encoder = payload_encoder
        self.clock = clock
        if research is not None:
            raise ContractViolation("unsupported_capability: registering research batches remains incomplete")
        self.research = NoAdditionalResearch()

    async def decide(self, snapshot: m.DecisionSnapshot) -> m.DecisionOutcome:
        return (await self.run_once(snapshot)).outcome

    async def run_once(
        self,
        snapshot: m.DecisionSnapshot,
        *,
        previous_assessment: m.SupplierAssessment | None = None,
        recorded_input_bytes: bytes = b"",
    ) -> OfflineDecisionTrace:
        raw_snapshot = canonical_json(snapshot)
        ref = snapshot.context.snapshot
        stages = []
        issues = []
        generations = []
        assessment = intents = batch = decision = rendered = validation = payload = None
        phase = "snapshot"
        started = self.clock.monotonic()

        def remaining():
            utc = (snapshot.budget.deadline_at - self.clock.utcnow()).total_seconds()
            compute = float(snapshot.budget.compute_limit_s) - (self.clock.monotonic() - started)
            return min(utc, compute)

        def available():
            if remaining() <= 0:
                raise ContractViolation("deadline_exhausted: offline decision budget exhausted")

        async def bounded(call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
            available()
            return await asyncio.wait_for(call(), timeout=remaining())

        def completed():
            stages.append(OfflineStage(name=phase, status="completed", issues=()))

        try:
            snapshot = m.DecisionSnapshot.model_validate_json(raw_snapshot)
            if snapshot.state.version != ref.state_version:
                raise ContractViolation("stale_state: decision state version differs from snapshot")
            context = snapshot.context
            if (
                case_contract_hash(context.case) != ref.case_contract_hash
                or context.evidence.as_of != context.as_of
                or context.as_of > self.clock.utcnow()
                or "sha256:" + semantic_hash(context.evidence.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"context_version"}))
                != ref.context_version
                or economic_fingerprint(context.economic) != context.economic.fingerprint
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("stale_state: stale or edited context projection")
            if any(i.severity == "error" for i in (*context.evidence.gaps, *context.economic.issues)) or any(
                c.blocking for c in context.evidence.conflicts
                c.blocking for c in context.evidence.conflicts
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("source_conflict: snapshot has unresolved evidence/economic errors")
            if snapshot.state.runtime_status not in ("ready", "deciding") or any(
                o.status in ("prepared", "submitted", "uncertain") for o in snapshot.state.operations
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("operation_pending: decision has unresolved ownership")
            if previous_assessment is not None and (
                previous_assessment.supplier_id != snapshot.target_supplier_id
                or previous_assessment.snapshot.run_id != ref.run_id
                or previous_assessment.snapshot.session_id != ref.session_id
                or previous_assessment.snapshot.state_version > ref.state_version
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("stale_state: previous assessment belongs to another/future state")
            available()
            completed()
            phase = "interpretation"
            assessment = await bounded(
                lambda: self.interpreter.interpret(
                    context,
                    snapshot.conversation,
                    previous_assessment,
                    snapshot.budget,
                )
            )
            assessment = m.SupplierAssessment.model_validate_json(assessment.model_dump_json())
            _assessment(assessment, snapshot)
            completed()
            phase = "proposal"
            intents = await bounded(
                lambda: self.proposal.propose_strategies(
                    context,
                    assessment,
                    snapshot.state,
                    snapshot.budget,
                    self.research,
                )
            )
            intents = m.IntentBatch.model_validate_json(intents.model_dump_json())
            if intents.snapshot != ref or not intents.intents or len(intents.intents) > snapshot.budget.candidate_limit:
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: proposal returned empty/oversized/stale intent batch")
            for intent in intents.intents:
                if intent.supplier_id != snapshot.target_supplier_id:
                    raise ContractViolation("scope_mismatch: proposed intent targets another supplier")
                if not set(intent.observation_refs) <= {o.observation_id for o in assessment.observations}:
                    raise ContractViolation("ungrounded_output: intent references unknown observation")
                for citation in intent.evidence_refs:
                    _citation(citation, snapshot)
            if any(i.severity == "error" for i in intents.issues):
                raise ContractViolation("infeasible: proposal contains unresolved errors")
            completed()
            phase = "generation"
            for intent in intents.intents:
                available()
                generated = self.generator.generate_candidates(intent, context, snapshot.state, snapshot.budget)
                generated = m.GenerationResult.model_validate_json(generated.model_dump_json())
                generations.append(generated)
                issues.extend(generated.rejections)
                if generated.intent_id != intent.intent_id or any(
                    c.intent_id != intent.intent_id
                    or c.supplier_id != snapshot.target_supplier_id
                    or c.snapshot != ref
                    or c.candidate_id != candidate_id(c)
                    for c in generated.candidates
                ):
                    raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: generator returned forged candidate/snapshot")
            candidates = tuple(c for g in generations for c in g.candidates)
            if not candidates or len(candidates) > min(20, snapshot.budget.candidate_limit):
                raise ContractViolation("infeasible: no candidates or global candidate budget exceeded")
            completed()
            phase = "evaluation"
            available()
            batch = self.evaluator.evaluate_candidates(candidates, context)
            batch = m.EvaluationBatch.model_validate_json(batch.model_dump_json())
            verify_batch(batch)
            if batch.snapshot != ref or {i.candidate.candidate_id: i.candidate for i in batch.items} != {
                c.candidate_id: c for c in candidates
            }:
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: evaluator changed registered candidate membership")
            issues.extend(i for item in batch.items for i in item.issues)
            completed()
            phase = "selection"
            decision = await bounded(
                lambda: self.selector.select_action(
                    batch,
                    assessment,
                    snapshot.state,
                    snapshot.budget,
                    self.research,
                )
            )
            decision = m.NegotiationDecision.model_validate_json(decision.model_dump_json())
            selected = next((i for i in batch.items if i.candidate.candidate_id == decision.candidate_id), None)
            if (
                selected is None
                or selected.disposition != "approved"
                or decision.snapshot != ref
                or decision.approved_batch_hash != batch.batch_hash
                or decision.evaluation_id != selected.evaluation_id
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: selection is not an approved registered batch member")
            for citation in decision.citations:
                _citation(citation, snapshot)
            completed()
            phase = "rendering"
            available()
            rendered = self.renderer_factory(batch).render(decision, selected, (), context)
            rendered = m.RenderedAction.model_validate_json(rendered.model_dump_json())
            contents = selected.candidate.contents
            expected_packages = contents.packages if isinstance(contents, m.OfferAction) else ()
            if (
                rendered.snapshot != ref
                or rendered.supplier_id != snapshot.target_supplier_id
                or rendered.decision_ref != "sha256:" + semantic_hash(decision)
                or rendered.kind != contents.kind
                or rendered.payload.packages != expected_packages
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: renderer edited the selected action")
            completed()
            phase = "validation"
            available()
            validation = self.validator.validate_action(rendered, context, snapshot.state, snapshot.budget)
            validation = TypeAdapter(m.ValidationResult).validate_json(validation.model_dump_json())
            if validation.kind == "invalid":
                issues.extend(validation.report.issues)
                raise ContractViolation("infeasible: independent used-action validation rejected selection")
            certificate = validation.action
            if (
                certificate.rendered != rendered
                or certificate.report.snapshot != ref
                or certificate.economic_fingerprint != context.economic.fingerprint
                or certificate.expires_at <= self.clock.utcnow()
                or certificate.expires_at > snapshot.budget.deadline_at
            ):
                raise ContractViolation("stale_state: validation certificate is expired or inconsistent")
            wire = self.payload_encoder(rendered.payload)
            if hashlib.sha256(wire).hexdigest() != certificate.payload_hash:
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: exact bytes differ from validated message")
            available()
            payload = wire
            completed()
            outcome = m.SelectedOutcome(kind="selected", decision=decision)
        except (ContractViolation, ValidationError, TimeoutError) as error:
            failure = _issue(error, "orchestration.offline:" + phase)
            issues.append(failure)
            stages.append(OfflineStage(name=phase, status="failed", issues=(failure,)))
            outcome = m.CannotDecideOutcome(kind="cannot_decide", snapshot=ref, issues=tuple(issues))
        trace = OfflineDecisionTrace(
            snapshot=ref,
            snapshot_bytes=raw_snapshot,
            recorded_input_bytes=recorded_input_bytes,
            input_hash=hashlib.sha256(recorded_input_bytes or raw_snapshot).hexdigest(),
            components=tuple(
                type(component).__module__ + "." + type(component).__qualname__
                for component in (
                    self.interpreter,
                    self.proposal,
                    self.generator,
                    self.evaluator,
                    self.selector,
                    self.validator,
                )
            ),
            stages=tuple(stages),
            assessment=assessment,
            intents=intents,
            generations=tuple(generations),
            evaluations=batch,
            decision=decision,
            rendered=rendered,
            validation=validation,
            validated_message_bytes=payload,
            issues=tuple(issues),
            outcome=outcome,
            trace_hash="0" * 64,
        )
        trace = trace.model_copy(
            update={"trace_hash": semantic_hash(trace.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"trace_hash"}))}
        )
        trace.verify()
        return trace
"}}

# A — Current architecture assessment and V2 migration map

**Status:** planning evidence, 10 October 2026. Inspecting `4c905b10be1f576de9b68be9c120cf6796ae4561`, not the main snapshot in document 18. [Plan and tracker](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md).

## 1. What is operational

The custom buyer is primarily deterministic. [PackageAgent](../../src/negotiator/agent.py) owns schedule, package memory, finals, evidence activation, estimator loading, and optional advice. `decide()` orchestrates serial thread choice; `propose()` provides thread proposals and reconstructs some memory. `_offer()` renders and logs before transmission and mutates `prev`; `_final_counter()` increments counters before acknowledgement. Those methods couple proposal generation to strategic state and observability.

[evaluator.py](../../src/negotiator/evaluator.py) provides `eligible_sheets`, `best_close`, `close_decision`, `supplier_for`, `price_for_cost`, and `revealed_deltas`. Complete arithmetic comes from official `arena_kit.cost`. Standing first sheets can be accepted; other sheets become counteroffer candidates. [optimizer.py](../../src/negotiator/optimizer.py) enumerates non-price options via `best_terms`. It does not model supplier acceptance. `plan` and `meso` are stubs, distinct from working payment variants in PackageAgent.

[EvidenceContext](../../src/negotiator/context.py) records relevant facts, source hashes, verified claim candidates, classifier signals and gaps. It is mutable and its `build_context` recursively hashes package files during construction. [EvidencePolicy](../../src/negotiator/evidence.py) decorates an already-generated offer, restricts eligible cases, and reserves IDs before a successful send. [claims.py](../../src/negotiator/claims.py) implements canonical rendering/checks, index windows, scorecard scope, notice scope, and disclosure rules. Evidence is usually not an input to baseline price/package strategy. Supplier-returned `claim_results` do not update selection.

[dossiers.py](../../src/negotiator/dossiers.py) uses base SQL for many attributes and should-cost estimates, with partial news/doc overlays. `_cost_row` does not give an existing case cost ID precedence over SQLite. Traits are regex-derived hypotheses; they are not known valuations. The estimator selects the first part, makes rate/margin assumptions, and exposes a range without live scenario optimization.

[PackageAdvisor](../../src/negotiator/package_advisor.py) is a functioning optional serial selector. `approved_packages` creates bounded one-field legal variants, applies a buyer-cost ceiling, and excludes previously sent packages. The model returns an ID and exact quote; code rechecks it and emits a template. It is not a general supplier interpreter or strategic memory system. Its timeout helper uses daemon threads that can outlive local waiting. [writer.py](../../src/negotiator/writer.py), [beliefs.py](../../src/negotiator/beliefs.py), and `policy.next_move` are unimplemented and have no normal execution path.

[play.py](../../src/negotiator/play.py) supplies custom serial closing and calls the new branch validator. Ordinary serial uses official `RemoteTable`/client; it is not a durable resumable decision system. [CaseRunner](../../src/negotiator/runner.py) has async tasks, journals, reconciliation, watchdog and closing. It accesses agent internals (`trades`, estimates, adviser capability), holds a lock over awaited proposal generation, and handles thread proposals and global economic closing in the same runtime module.

[state.py](../../src/negotiator/state.py) has fsynced JSONL operation intents and mutable runtime state. It preserves `unresolved` intents on this branch and repairs torn trailing journal records. It is not a versioned persistent strategic event store. [trace.py](../../src/negotiator/trace.py) is append-only diagnostic JSONL, not transactional state; [report.py](../../src/negotiator/report.py) follows `decision` events rather than one final acknowledged-action record.

The [Lab](../../src/negotiator/lab) is substantial implemented infrastructure: strict run/attempt records, checkpoints, data fingerprints, campaign leases/budget gates, stores, comparison, reconciliation, publication buffering, and UI. `lab.runner.agent_factory` constructs PackageAgent directly; `lab.worker.execute` hardcodes it; `lab.checkpoints.resolve_config` accepts a narrower set of settings. They do not automatically reproduce normal CLI guidance and adviser activation. The Lab dashboard deployment is separate from buyer execution and inference.

## 2. Actual flow and coupling

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CLI[CLI guidance and policy] --> PA[PackageAgent]
    LAB[Lab direct factories] --> PA
    CASE[Case and thread dictionaries] --> PA
    SQL[Base SQL dossiers] --> EST[Optional estimates]
    EST --> PA
    PA --> OPT[Optimizer and evaluator]
    PA --> TRADE[Optional deterministic trades]
    PA --> EV[Optional evidence decoration]
    FACT[Facts and partial overlays] --> EV
    PA --> ADV[Optional serial package adviser]
    ADV --> RUN[Serial or async runner]
    EV --> RUN
    PA --> RUN
    RUN --> GUARD[Branch validator]
    GUARD --> HTTP[Arena client]
    HTTP --> CASE
    RUN --> CLOSE[Shared closing evaluator]
    RUN --> JOURNAL[Journal and trace]
    PA --> JOURNAL
    JOURNAL --> REPORT[Lab and reports]
```

Important seams to replace:

| Coupling | Consequence | V2 boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `PackageAgent` mutates memory while proposing | Failed/unsent moves can affect next choice | Pure decision inputs; attempted-state changes only from committed/acknowledged events |
| Evidence/estimates use different data access paths | Same cost/source can mean different things | One layered typed resolver; projections for claims and estimates |
| Runtime discovers features using agent attributes | Launch path alters feature availability | Resolved capabilities and `DecisionEngine` contract |
| Model choice occurs after ordinary offer logging | Reports show an earlier candidate | Final rendered payload and economics linked to decision and operation IDs |
| Closing arithmetic assumes helper behavior and weak outgoing checks | Current standing ID alone does not prove legality | Independent economic service and final validator |
| State is a mix of dictionaries, timers and agent fields | Restart loses refusal/hold/challenge context | Server projection plus durable strategic events |
| Advisory calls use environment and internal caches | Config/cancellation/comparability differ | Injected model gateway, explicit prompt/config version and call budget |

## 3. Current-to-V2 component migration map

“Reuse” means retain a tested implementation behind a new contract, not assume every caller is safe. No code moves are part of this plan.

| Existing component / symbols | Decision | Target | Justification and required adaptation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official `cost_breakdown`, `total_cost`, `closing_terms`, `must_haves_ok` | Retain and wrap | `v2/economics/official.py` | Scoring arithmetic remains pinned; validate inputs, retain per-component results and scenario provenance |
| Official `complete_offer`, `snap` | Restricted use | `v2/economics/candidates.py` | Useful for trusted construction only; never silently repair supplier/model output |
| `optimizer.best_terms` enumeration | Extract algorithm | `v2/economics/candidates.py` | Finite combinations are useful; bound cardinality, legal standards exception, explicit infeasibility and deterministic ties |
| `evaluator.price_for_cost` | Replace dependency | `v2/economics/prices.py` | Ordinary rounded-cost regression and unreliable relationship roots; initial relationship candidates use a bounded tick set with final certification |
| `eligible_sheets`, `best_close`, `close_decision` | Extract policy and strengthen | `v2/economics/closing.py` | One close comparison is sound; add complete legality, recipient/session ownership, fresh snapshot, typed no-alternative and estimate scenarios |
| `supplier_for` quote merge | Retain behavior and test | `v2/economics/estimates.py` | Current quote fields override master estimates; standards provenance and partial fields remain explicit |
| `revealed_deltas` | Extract observation primitive | `v2/intelligence/feedback.py` | One-field observations useful; multi-field changes stay combined; do not infer causal valuation or willingness |
| `claims.Claim`, `render`, `check`, `verify`, `claim_keys` | Wrap, then adapt resolver | `v2/evidence/claims.py` | Canonical checks useful; remove duplicate SQL/first-part joins, share basis/scope, support durable usage ledger |
| `claims.pick`, `EvidencePolicy.eligible/enrich` | Replace orchestration | `v2/evidence/claims.py` and strategy | Optional claims can affect intent selection; retain conservative disclosure, avoid premature usage consumption |
| `context.build_context`, hashes/gaps | Retain concepts; replace model and hot-path hashing | `v2/evidence/context.py`, `prepare.py` | Layered immutable snapshot, prebuilt indexes, typed conflict/freshness and part scope |
| `DataPackage`, official PDF/XLSX readers | Retain and wrap | `v2/adapters/data.py`, evidence documents | Preserve bytes/parse provenance; explicit roots/releases, SQL overlay limitations, formula strings not recalculated |
| `dossiers._cost_row`, `supplier_estimate`, `for_case` | Replace resolver; reuse documented calculations selectively | Evidence resolver + estimate service | Fix precedence, scope, case letters/news replacement and uncertainty; do not export legacy dossiers as truth |
| `traits.classify/evidence` | Optional legacy feature extractor | Interpreter deterministic fallback | Keep source links and label hypotheses; no automatic trait-to-contract binding |
| PackageAgent schedule | Preserve V1; extract pure baseline when needed | `v2/strategy/baseline.py` | Comparable deterministic fallback; do not call stateful internals from V2 strategy modules |
| `TradePolicy` | Keep V1; port isolated tested rules later | `v2/strategy/capacity.py` initially | No expansion of V1 conditional tree; new strategy emits typed intents |
| `PackageAdvisor` schema/ID/quote pattern | Reuse design; replace implementation coupling | Interpreter/selector + model adapter | Grounded structured outputs and ID choice useful; inject async cancellable gateway, persist assessments, separate interpreting from selecting |

# Multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) reduce the negotiator dilemma: How a choice of first offers increases economic and relational outcomes

Author links open overlay panel Geoffrey J. Leonardelli ^{a}, Jun Gu ^{b}, Geordie McRuer ^{c}, Victoria Husted Medvec ^{d}, Adam D. Galinsky ^{e}

## Highlights

  * •

Six experiments found first-offer choice (MESOs) increased offerer and joint outcomes.

  * •

First-offer choice produced greater agreement sincerity and initial recipient-value.

  * •

Agreement sincerity mediated MESOs’ effects on offerer outcomes.

  * •

Initial recipient-value mediated MESOs’ effects on joint outcomes.

  * •

Offering choice created a cooperative reputation and positive negotiation climate.

## Abstract

The tension that negotiators face between claiming and creating value is particularly apparent when exchanging offers. We tested whether presenting a choice among first offers (Multiple Equivalent Simultaneous Offers; MESOs) reduces this negotiator dilemma and increases economic and relational outcomes. Six experiments comparing MESOs to a single package-offer revealed three effects. First, MESOs produced stronger anchors and better outcomes for the offerer because recipients perceived MESOs as a more sincere attempt at reaching an agreement (agreement sincerity). Second, MESOs yielded greater joint outcomes because they were probabilistically more likely to include an economically attractive starting point for recipients (initial recipient-value). Third, MESOs allowed the offerer to secure a cooperative reputation and created a more cooperative negotiation climate. Negotiators who offered MESOs were able to claim and create more economic and relational value. MESOs reduced the negotiator dilemma for offerers by also reducing it for recipients. Weblinks in the appendix give access to supplementary materials, analyses, and data.

## Abstract

We present a formal model of negotiation between autonomous agents. The purpose of the negotiation is to reach an agreement about the provision of a service by one agent for another. The model defines a range of strategies and tactics that agents can employ to generate initial offers, evaluate proposals and offer counter proposals. The model is based on computationally tractable assumptions, demonstrated in the domain of business process management and empirically evaluated.

clude a choice of two or more package offers to the recipient and
equivalence denotes that, although each offer presents a different set of

single package-offer, we propose that MESOs as first offers will reduce

more favorable economic and relational outcomes. They will do so, we
argue, in part by reducing the recipients’ experience of their own ne-
gotiator dilemma.

SCALE = 0.004  # 1 simulated second = 4 ms; the 60 s rule takes 0.24 s


class ScaledClock(Clock):
    def __init__(self, scale=SCALE):
        self.scale, self.t0, self.m0 = scale, time.time(), time.monotonic()

    def time(self):
        return self.t0 + (time.monotonic() - self.m0) / self.scale

    async def sleep(self, s):
        await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, s) * self.scale)


class SimArena:
    """AsyncArena's interface over the kit simulator: X-Move-Id idempotency, supplier reply
    delays that do not count against the buyer (as hosted), and one-shot fault injection."""

    def __init__(self, clock, delays=None):
        self.clock, self.delays = clock, delays or {}
        self.sim = Sim(load_cases(), clock=clock.time)
        self.team, self.replies, self.opens, self.posts = "t", {}, 0, []
        self.fail_next_close = None  # an ArenaError status to raise once on the next close POST
        self.lose_reply = False  # next send lands but the reply is lost (UncertainOutcome)

    def _do(self, fn, *a):
        try:
            return fn(self.team, *a)

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from arena_kit.cost import complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost


@dataclass
class Plan:
    c_alt: float  # alternative's C (inf if none)
    c_open: float  # cheapest opening quote's C
    reservation_c: float  # walk-away: never accept above this
    target_c: float  # where we aim
    best_nonprice: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # cheapest values for non-price fields
    concession_path: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)  # target C per round
    supplier_estimate: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # full_cost, interest_rate, standard


def plan(case: dict, standard_terms: dict, dossier=None) -> Plan:
    """Reservation, target and concession path. In stabilise/secure_supply, include the
    relationship term with a supplier estimate (should-cost ± sensitivity)."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def meso(case: dict, anchor: dict, c_target: float, n: int = 3) -> list[dict]:
    """n complete term sheets with (nearly) equal C for us but different mixes
    (price-heavy, payment-heavy, term/volume-heavy). Uses arena_kit.cost.complete_offer."""
    raise NotImplementedError


def alternative_cost(case: dict) -> float:
    alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
    terms = alt.get("terms") or {}
    return total_cost(case, terms) if terms.get("unit_price") else float("inf")


def best_terms(case: dict, unit_price: float, standard: dict | None = None, supplier=None,
               prefer_longer_lead: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Complete term sheet at `unit_price` whose non-price fields minimise C and keep the
    must-haves. Fields without listed options keep the buyer's plan (`complete_offer`)."""
    base = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": unit_price})
    options = case.get("term_options") or {}
    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price" and options.get(f)]
    best, best_c = None, float("inf")
    for combo in itertools.product(*(options[f] for f in fields)):
        terms = {**base, **dict(zip(fields, combo, strict=True))}
        if not must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard):
            continue
        c = total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)
        same_cost_longer_lead = (
            prefer_longer_lead and "lead_time_days" in fields and c == best_c
            and terms["lead_time_days"] > best["lead_time_days"]
        )
        if c < best_c or same_cost_longer_lead:
            best, best_c = terms, c
    return best


def payment_breakeven_pct(case: dict, from_days: int, to_days: int) -> float:
    """Exact price discount (%) offsetting the buyer's payment-timing value.

    Payment timing is compared with the case reference term. This preserves the
    complete-cost ratio when neither endpoint is itself the reference term.
    """
    buyer = case["buyer"]
    r = buyer["interest_rate"]
    reference = buyer.get("reference_payment_days", 60)
    from_factor = 1 + r * (reference - from_days) / 360
    to_factor = 1 + r * (reference - to_days) / 360
    if to_factor <= 0:
        raise ValueError("payment term produces a non-positive discount factor")
    return (1 - from_factor / to_factor) * 100

L62@P1: find evidence of sophisticated negotiation strategies. For example, we find instances of the model
L63@P1: feigning interest in a valueless issue, so that it can
L64@P1: later ‘compromise’ by conceding it. Deceit is a

L67@P1: development (Talwar and Lee, 2002). Our agents

L71@P1: be improved by goal-based training (§4) and decoding (§5). §6 measures the performance of our
L72@P1: models and humans on this task, and §7 gives a
L73@P1: detailed analysis and suggests future directions.
L74@P1: 2 Data Collection
L75@P1: 2.1 Overview
L76@P1: To enable end-to-end training of negotiation
L77@P1: agents, we first develop a novel negotiation task
L78@P1: and curate a dataset of human-human dialogues
L79@P1: for this task. This task and dataset follow our
L80@P1: proposed general framework for studying semicooperative dialogue. Initially, each agent is
L81@P1: shown an input specifying a space of possible actions and a reward function which will score the
L82@P1: outcome of the negotiation. Agents then sequentially take turns of either sending natural language
L83@P1: messages, or selecting that a final decision has
L84@P1: been reached. When one agent selects that an
L85@P1: agreement has been made, both agents independently output what they think the agreed decision
L86@P1: was. If conflicting decisions are made, both agents
L87@P1: are given zero reward.
L88@P1: 2.2 Task
L89@P1: Our task is an instance of multi issue bargaining
L90@P1: (Fershtman, 1990), and is based on DeVault et al.
L91@P1: (2015). Two agents are both shown the same collection of items, and instructed to divide them so
L92@P1: that each item assigned to one agent.
L93@P1: Each agent is given a different randomly generated value function, which gives a non-negative
L94@P1: value for each item. The value functions are constrained so that: (1) the total value for a user of
L95@P1: all items is 10; (2) each item has non-zero value
L96@P1: to at least one user; and (3) some items have nonzero value to both users. These constraints enforce
L97@P1: that it is not possible for both agents to receive a
L98@P1: maximum score, and that no item is worthless to
L99@P1: both agents, so the negotiation will be competitive.

L101@P1: worth 0 points to both users. We use 3 item types

L103@P1: items in the pool. Figure 1 shows our interface.

Validation returns issues, never repaired prices or packages. Test it directly without engine/runtime, then assert every supported execution path calls it with the final payload, including questions, fallback, close and replay admission.

### State and feedback contract

`apply_event` is pure and rejects invalid sequence/session/schema transitions. `load_state` projects the latest valid snapshot plus subsequent events. `persist_state` is the atomic expected-version commit boundary; callers cannot persist arbitrary altered server status. Assessment/decision artifacts can be stored without advancing the negotiation head; committing their strategic meaning and operation together advances local sequence, avoiding self-invalidating snapshots.

Store assigns contiguous sequence under transaction; unique `(run,event_id)` and official source keys deduplicate repeats. Out-of-order message arrivals are recorded with original server order/ref, then reconciled before new decisions. Duplicate event application is idempotent by ID; mismatched contents for one source key create a conflict. Persist UTC/server evidence and derive local elapsed time with Clock. Claim reservations/attempts move to submitted/acknowledged based on proven execution events, not strategy calls.

Feedback returns EventProposals and writes nothing. It joins operation/decision/candidate/response, records actual package differences (single-field or combined), explicit question-response linkage, claim-result alignment and structured observed support/contradiction. Semantic refusal/answer/support attribution comes from the next validated assessment, not an unimplemented deterministic understanding of arbitrary prose; applying `AssessmentRecorded` produces the source-linked strategic refusal revision. A later price reduction is an observation, not an estimated causal effect of an argument. Refusals and source messages survive restart. Startup does not forget unsupported events; it refuses unsafe projection and preserves files for diagnosis.

### Executor, recovery and gateway contract

The executor does not change the selected strategy, packages, claims or wording. It accepts only a validator-issued action linked to a committed operation and valid dispatch permit. Exact canonical payload bytes/hash and logical ID are persisted before any POST. It verifies permit/state/context/economic freshness after limiter queue; for first serial scope the coordinator retains ownership while awaiting transport. New server observations invalidate unsent stale permits.
